text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes is diagnosed using specific blood tests that measure your blood glucose or average blood sugar levels over time.
snippet_highlighted_words: using specific blood tests that measure your blood glucose or average blood sugar levels over time

text_blocks.snippet: Doctors diagnose type 2 diabetes using any of the following standard lab tests:

list.snippet: Hemoglobin A1C Test: Measures your average blood sugar over the past 2 to 3 months.
Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) Test: Measures your blood sugar after you have not eaten or drunk anything except water for at least 8 hours.
Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT): Measures your blood sugar before and 2 hours after you drink a special sugary liquid (75-gram glucose drink).
Diabetes: 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or higher at the 2-hour mark
Prediabetes: 140 to 199 mg/dL at the 2-hour mark
Random Plasma Glucose Test: Measures your blood sugar at any time of day.
Diabetes: 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or higher — only if you also have classic symptoms of high blood sugar (such as frequent urination, extreme thirst, or unexplained weight loss).

Retesting: Unless you have very high blood sugar or clear, severe symptoms, doctors generally require a repeat test on a second day (or two different tests from the same blood draw) to confirm the diagnosis.

Screening Guidelines: The American Diabetes Association recommends routine screening for all adults starting at age 35, or earlier if you have risk factors like overweight/obesity, a family history of diabetes, or high blood pressure.
